text:
emma: FYI mkdocs deploy failed on prod: a bunch of anchors 404ing after the mdx include refactor. https://ci.redwood/infer-build/17665/logs

jia: ugh ok. is this the same include reorder we landed yesterday?

emma: yeah, PR #4219 — I see local build passes but CI linkcheck flags fragments. deploy-bot posted the diff in the logs.

sam: small checklist: 1) did the include change headings (h2->h3) 2) slugify differences between docusaurus vs mkdocs 3) relative path canonicalization

marta: @sam re: slugify — mkdocs ascii-folding strips emoji and some punctuation, mdx inline HTML leaves raw ids. could produce different anchors for the same heading.

emma: here's a repro: in the page we include a snippet file that has a heading `## Usage (beta) :sparkles:`. mkdocs slug becomes `usage-beta` but the reference in another page uses `usage-(beta)` so the fragment breaks.

jia: ahhh emoji in heading. recommended fix: remove emoji in the generated heading or add explicit header id e.g. `## Usage {#usage-beta}` in the snippet.

sam: or normalize the cross-page link to the slug produced by mkdocs. but that requires us to know renderer slug rules. better to add explicit ids in the snippet to be stable across toolchains.

marta: quick patch: add explicit id to the snippet and add a tiny test in the docs CI that runs mkdocs linkcheck + a slug normalize step. I'll open a followup PR.

emma: cool. can someone push the snippet fix to #4219 so the failing deploy can be unblocked?

jia: pushing quick commit now. patch is just: in examples/quickstart.md snippet -> change `## Usage (beta) :sparkles:` to `## Usage {#usage-beta}` and remove emoji.

deploy-bot: build triggered for branch docs/fix-snippet-usage -> running linkcheck + mkdocs build

sam: also add a one-line note in the migration guide about heading id stability when migrating from docusaurus -> mkdocs. had a couple surprises when we changed slugify libs.

emma: agreed — add to docs/migration/docusaurus-to-mkdocs.md under "Headings & Anchors" with the explicit id recommendation and a short command to find problematic headings: `rg "[:emoji:]|\(|\)" docs/ | sed -n '1,200p'` (very rough).

marta: PR opened: #4221 — includes snippet id + migration note + tiny CI linkcheck tweak (retry flaky network). tagging @emma @sam for review.

emma: quick review done, left one nit about the sed example. otherwise thumbs up. :thumbsup:

jia: CI is green on the patch branch, deploy requeued.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: prod docs site updated (yay).

sam: nice. follow-up: create a lint rule in docs pre-commit to warn on emoji in headings and suggest `{#id}`. low pri but will save future headaches.

marta: will add to the backlog and maybe do a small precommit hook.

emma: thanks all. saved the morning. :coffee:

marta: note for posterity: tag in the release notes that we changed include handling; some older external links might 404 until authors add explicit ids.

sam: filed internal FYI ticket for that.

emma: closing thread once the deploy bot confirms prod.

deploy-bot: final status: success, linkcheck warnings only (no broken fragments).
